div.l: That eche of you to shorte wyth your weye
In this vyage shall telle talys tweye
To caunterbury warde I meane it so
And hom warde he shall telle other tales two
Of auentures that whylom haue befalle
And whyche of you beryth hym best of alle
That is to saye that tellyth in this caas
Tales of best sentence and most solaas
Shall haue a supper of our alther cost
Here in this place syttynge by this post
Whan that we come ayen from Caunterbury
And for to make you the more mery
I wyll myself goodly wyth you ryde
Ryght at myn owne coste and be your guyde
And who that woll my Iugement wythsay
Shortly shal paye all that is spent by the way
And yf ye vouchesauf that it be soo
Telle me anone wythout wordes moo
And I woll erly shape me therfore
This thynge was graunted and othes swore
Wyth full glad herte and prayen hym also
That he wolde vouchesauf that it be so
And that he wolde be our gouernour
And of our tales Iuge ⁊and reportour
And sette a supper at a certayn pryce
And wolde be ruled at his deuyce
Hyghe and lowe and all by one assent
We be accorded to his Iugement
And there vpon the wyne was fet anone
We dronke and to rest went we echon
Wythout ony lenger taryenge
A morow whan the day gan sprynge
Vp rose our host and was all our cocke
And gadred vs togyder all in a flocke
And forth we ryden lytyll more than paas
Vnto the watrynge of saynt thomas
And there our host gan his hors areste
And sayd herkenyth lordynges yf ye lyste
Ye wote our forwarde and I you recorde
Yf euesonge and morow songe acorde
Let se now who shall telle the fyrste tale
As euer moot I drynke wyne or ale
Who so woll be rebell to my Iugement
Shall paye for all that is by the waye spent
NOw drawe cut or that ye further twynne
Whiche shall the fyrst tale begynne
Syre knyght quod he my mayster ⁊and my lorde
Now draweth cut for that is myn accorde
Come hyther quod he my lady pryoresse
And ye syre clerke lete by your shamfastnesse
Ne study not lay on honde euery man
And on to drawe euery wyght began
And shortly to telle as it was
Were it by auenture fortune or caas
The soth is thus the cut fell on the knyght
Of whyche full blythe ⁊and glad is euery wyght
And tell he must as it was reson
By forwarde and by composycion
As ye haue herde what nedyth wordes moo
And whan this good man sawe that it was soo
As he that was wyse and obedyent
To kepe his forwarde by his free assent
He sayd sythnes I shall begynne the game
What welcom be cut a goddis name
Now lete vs ryde and herken what I say
And with that worde we ryden forth our way
And he began wyth ryght a mery chere
And sayd anone his tale as ye shall here
Here begynnyth the knyghtis tale
